findings.statement: Before buying, the buyer asked specifically about box condition and said it was most of what they were paying for, and the seller answered that the boxes were fine and the sets had been stored in a cupboard since new.
The listing described four retired sets as used, like new, with boxes in good condition, at a price of 200.
The parcel was delivered on 28 August, and the buyer reported a badly crushed and split box corner the same afternoon, a few hours later.
The photograph of the set shows one box with a crushed and split upper corner and scuffing along the edges; the rest of the box front appears sound.
The seller maintains the item was in good condition when it left them and was packed carefully; no photograph of the packing or of the sets before posting has been provided.
Only one of the four sets is pictured, so nothing in the file speaks to the condition of the other three boxes.

provisional.reasoning: The seller gave a clear assurance about box condition in answer to a direct question, and one of the four boxes arrived with a crushed, split corner. Since box condition was a stated part of what was being paid for, a partial refund reflecting the damage to one box out of four is fair, with the contents and the other three boxes apparently unaffected.

requests.what: One photograph of the outer shipping package the sets arrived in — the whole carton, including any padding or filling still inside it, so its condition and how the sets were packed can be seen.
requests.whyItMatters: You and the seller disagree about how the corner came to be crushed: whether it happened after the parcel left the seller or before. The state of the outer package and what was used to pad the sets inside it is the one thing that can tell those two accounts apart, and nobody has photographed it yet.

wouldChange.answer: The outer package shows heavy crushing or a hole at the corresponding corner, with padding present inside
wouldChange.implies: The damage happened in transit despite reasonable packing; the seller's assurance was honest but the buyer still received a box that is not as described

wouldChange.answer: The outer package is intact and undamaged, or the sets were sent with little or no padding
wouldChange.implies: The damage was either already present when posted or caused by the way it was packed, both of which sit with the seller against their assurance that the boxes were fine
The case rests on the single photograph of the damaged box and the seller's pre-sale assurance
